problemTracks.statementMarkdown:
### Theme 1 — Biomedical Artificial Intelligence

**Society:** IEEE EMBS × IEEE CIS | **Track:** Advanced | **Technique:** Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search & Hybrid GA-ML

#### Context
Clinical healthcare pipelines generate vast multi-modal patient telemetry, electronic health records, genomic biomarkers, and pathology features. Medical practitioners require explainable AI models capable of predictive risk stratification while respecting strict sensitivity constraints.

#### Core Challenge
Design an evolutionary optimization algorithm to search high-dimensional biomedical feature spaces and optimize hybrid clinical decision boundaries, maximizing sensitivity for rare critical pathologies while minimizing false positive alerts under real-world clinical noise.

#### Hard Constraints
- Sensitivity for life-critical conditions must exceed 98%.
- Selected features must maintain causal and physiological plausibility.
- Diagnostic predictions must provide calibrated uncertainty intervals.
- Execution latency must adhere to real-time clinical screening SLAs.
- Pipeline must handle missing clinical covariates gracefully.

#### Optimization Objectives
Maximize diagnostic ROC-AUC, minimize false alarm fatigue, minimize parameter complexity, and maximize generalization across heterogeneous patient populations.
problemTracks.hiddenShiftAttempt2: Demographic perturbation: Patient age and comorbid distributions shifted by 35% with missing laboratory markers.
problemTracks.hiddenShiftAttempt3: Adversarial clinical noise: 20% of continuous ICU vitals perturbed with Gaussian sensor drift.
problemTracks.livePatchSurprise: One urgent biomarker feature is rendered unavailable; algorithm must dynamically re-evaluate confidence without retraining from scratch.

### Theme 4 — Neurotechnology & Rehabilitation

#### Context
Assistive neuroprosthetics and robotic rehabilitation exoskeletons decode noisy neural signals to restore motor function for post-stroke and spinal cord injury patients undergoing therapy.

#### Core Challenge
Develop a swarm-optimized adaptive decoding algorithm that converts non-stationary neural intent and muscular EMG telemetry into smooth, jerk-free therapeutic robotic trajectories under non-linear muscle fatigue.

- Biomechanical joint torque limits must never be exceeded.
- End-to-end decoding latency must remain strictly below 50ms.
- Adaptive calibration must track ongoing electrode impedance drift.
- Trajectory jerk must comply with rehabilitation comfort standards.
- Fail-safe posture locking upon telemetry disconnection.

#### Optimization Objectives
Maximize motion decoding accuracy, minimize patient fatigue, maximize task precision, and ensure ultra-fast online adaptation.

### Theme 6 — Biomedical Signals & Intelligent Systems

**Society:** IEEE EMBS × IEEE CIS | **Track:** Intermediate–Advanced | **Technique:** Fuzzy Inference Systems + Evolutionary Signal Decomposition

#### Context
Intensive care units stream continuous multi-channel physiological signals (ECG, PPG, EEG, arterial pressure) where baseline wander, patient motion, and electrosurgical interference trigger frequent false alarms.

#### Core Challenge
Formulate an evolutionary fuzzy system that filters non-stationary artifacts, extracts morphological signal components, and detects acute cardiac or neurological events with high fidelity and ultra-low latency.

#### Hard Constraints
- Processing throughput must sustain continuous 500Hz multi-lead streaming.
- Lethal arrhythmias must trigger alarms within 2 seconds of onset.
- Fuzzy membership bounds must respect cardiology diagnostic criteria.
- Morphological QRS fiducial point fidelity must be preserved.
- Zero phase distortion in digital filtering stages.

#### Optimization Objectives
Drastically eliminate false alarm fatigue, maximize morphological SNR, minimize battery power draw, and guarantee 100% critical sensitivity.

**Society:** IEEE EMBS × IEEE CIS | **Track:** Intermediate–Advanced | **Technique:** Ant Colony Optimization + Energy-Aware Swarm Routing

#### Context
Hospital campuses deploy hundreds of battery-operated wearable biomedical sensors, smart infusion pumps, and environmental monitors transmitting vital health data over mesh IoT networks with limited bandwidth and battery reserves.

Design an Ant Colony Optimization routing protocol that balances transmission energy consumption, vital data packet priority, and network lifetime while guaranteeing deterministic latency for critical patient alerts.

Maximize IoT mesh operational longevity, minimize alert latency, minimize packet dropping, and optimize routing protocol efficiency.
